\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مخارج} (makhârej)}{مخارج (makhârej)}]{\fa{مخارج} (makhârej) — expenses, costs}

\label{lesson:FA-C415-makharej}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to withdraw, then the Persian for to transfer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مخارج}}
\textbf{\fa{مخارج}} (\emph{makhârej}) — \textquotedblleft{}expenses, costs\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مخارج} \fa{زندگی} \fa{هر} \fa{سال} \fa{بیشتر} \fa{میشود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{makhârej-e zendegi har sâl bishtar mishavad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cost of living goes up every year.
\end{quote}

A plural built in the Arabic way beside \emph{kharj} \textquotedblleft{}expense\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مخارج}} is an Arabic-style plural that Persian uses beside \emph{kharj} \textquotedblleft{}expense\textquotedblright{}; it is usually traced to an Arabic plural from the same family.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to withdraw, then the Persian for to transfer, then say \emph{makhârej} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صورتحساب} (surathesâb)}{صورتحساب (surathesâb)}]{\fa{صورتحساب} (surathesâb) — a bill, a statement}

\label{lesson:FA-C415-surathesab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to transfer, then the Persian for expenses.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صورتحساب}}
\textbf{\fa{صورتحساب}} (\emph{surathesâb}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bill, a statement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{شام} \fa{صورتحساب} \fa{را} \fa{آوردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ba'd az shâm surathesâb râ âvardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After dinner they brought the bill.
\end{quote}

\emph{Surat} \textquotedblleft{}form, list\textquotedblright{} + \emph{hesâb} \textquotedblleft{}account\textquotedblright{}. Also a bank statement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{صورتحساب}} is a Persian compound of two words from Arabic: \emph{surat}, from \emph{ṣūra} \textquotedblleft{}form\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), and \emph{hesâb}, from \emph{ḥisāb} \textquotedblleft{}reckoning, account\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to transfer, then the Persian for expenses, then say \emph{surathesâb} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کارمزد} (kârmozd)}{کارمزد (kârmozd)}]{\fa{کارمزد} (kârmozd) — a fee, a commission}

\label{lesson:FA-C415-karmozd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for expenses, then the Persian for a bill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کارمزد}}
\textbf{\fa{کارمزد}} (\emph{kârmozd}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fee, a commission\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بانک} \fa{برای} \fa{هر} \fa{انتقال} \fa{کارمزد} \fa{میگیرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bânk barâye har enteqâl kârmozd migirad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bank charges a fee for every transfer.
\end{quote}

\emph{Kâr} \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{} + \emph{mozd} \textquotedblleft{}wage\textquotedblright{}: pay for a service.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{کارمزد}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{kâr} \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{} + \emph{mozd} \textquotedblleft{}wage\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{mizd}: the wage for a piece of work.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{درصد} (darsad)}{درصد (darsad)}]{\fa{درصد} (darsad) — a percent, a percentage}

\label{lesson:FA-C415-darsad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bill, then the Persian for a fee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{درصد}}
\textbf{\fa{درصد}} (\emph{darsad}) — \textquotedblleft{}a percent, a percentage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پنجاه} \fa{درصد} \fa{مردم} \fa{رای} \fa{دادند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{panjâh darsad-e mardom ra'y dâdand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Fifty percent of the people voted.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} + \emph{sad} \textquotedblleft{}hundred\textquotedblright{}: per hundred.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{درصد}} is a native Persian compound, literally \textquotedblleft{}in a hundred\textquotedblright{}: \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} + \emph{sad} \textquotedblleft{}hundred\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB lists without a parent and which is usually traced to PIE \emph{*kmtom} \textquotedblleft{}hundred\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ولخرج} (velkharj)}{ولخرج (velkharj)}]{\fa{ولخرج} (velkharj) — a spendthrift; extravagant}

\label{lesson:FA-C415-velkharj}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fee, then the Persian for a percent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ولخرج}}
\textbf{\fa{ولخرج}} (\emph{velkharj}) — \textquotedblleft{}a spendthrift; extravagant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برادرم} \fa{خیلی} \fa{ولخرج} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{barâdaram kheyli velkharj ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother spends money too freely.
\end{quote}

\emph{Vel} \textquotedblleft{}loose\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kharj} \textquotedblleft{}spending\textquotedblright{}. Colloquial. \emph{Velkharji kardan} — to splash out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ولخرج}} joins the Persian word \emph{vel} \textquotedblleft{}loose, let go\textquotedblright{} to \emph{kharj} \textquotedblleft{}spending\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{kharj} \textquotedblleft{}outlay\textquotedblright{}: someone whose money runs loose.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
